answer: Rank identities by trust propagation: short random walks run through the attestation graph from several slow-moving seed sets of long-lived agents. A sybil farmer can stitch a dense internal web, but every walk must cross a genuine edge from the established region, and fresh bridge edges carry no pigment of trust until both endpoints age. One fabricated fable — a single thin thread to the honest economy — lets only a trickle through. Each new head needs its own costly edge, so N heads cost N real relationships, and the farm becomes indistinguishable from honest participation.
